# Hive

> Hive is an open-source (MIT) terminal multiplexer for AI coding agents, written in Rust. It runs Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and other agent CLIs side by side in real terminals on Linux, macOS and Windows, shows which agent is working, needs input or is done, and keeps sessions running in a local daemon (hived) when the terminal closes.

Install on Linux or macOS: `curl -fsSL https://github.com/jrh89/hive/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh`
Install on Windows (PowerShell): `irm 'https://github.com/jrh89/hive/releases/latest/download/install.ps1' | iex`
Source: https://github.com/jrh89/hive

## Docs

- [Features](https://hive.codefrontlabs.com/features/): live agent status, persistent sessions, spaces, git worktrees, panes, tabs, palette, keys, themes, platforms
- [Install](https://hive.codefrontlabs.com/install/): installers for Linux, macOS and Windows, upgrading and uninstalling
- [Integrations](https://hive.codefrontlabs.com/integrations/): Obsidian, lazygit review, GitHub PR checks, tasks, notifications, git status, usage, layouts, with config.toml snippets
- [Why Hive](https://hive.codefrontlabs.com/why/): comparison with tmux, Zellij and herdr
- [Changelog](https://hive.codefrontlabs.com/changelog/): every release
- [Documentation](https://hive.codefrontlabs.com/docs/): the full docs, also as a single file: [user guide](https://github.com/jrh89/hive/blob/master/docs/user-guide.md)
  - [Getting started](https://hive.codefrontlabs.com/docs/getting-started/): Install Hive, open it, start your first AI coding agents, detach and come back. The concepts you need: daemon, sessions, spaces, worktrees.
  - [The interface](https://hive.codefrontlabs.com/docs/interface/): What the sidebar, tab bar, status symbols and marks mean, how panes, tabs and spaces work, the mouse, and using Hive from several windows.
  - [Keys](https://hive.codefrontlabs.com/docs/keys/): Every Hive command with its default key after Ctrl+Space, the prefix-free Alt chords, and how to rebind or unbind any of them in config.toml.
  - [Configuration](https://hive.codefrontlabs.com/docs/configuration/): Every config.toml option with its type and default: general, terminal, daemon, notifications, integrations, worktrees, theme, keys, agents and layouts.
  - [Command line](https://hive.codefrontlabs.com/docs/cli/): Every hive command and option: new, list, attach, kill, agents, workspace, worktree, report-agent, doctor, update and daemon, with examples.
  - [Agent status](https://hive.codefrontlabs.com/docs/agent-status/): How Hive knows an agent is working, needs input or is done, which agents it recognises, the bell and notifications, and how scripts report their own status.
  - [Workspaces and worktrees](https://hive.codefrontlabs.com/docs/worktrees/): How Hive groups sessions into spaces by repository, and gives an agent its own git worktree and branch, with the rules that keep your work safe.
  - [Daemon, files and environment](https://hive.codefrontlabs.com/docs/daemon/): What hived does, what survives a crash or reboot, where Hive keeps its files, the environment variables it reads and sets, upgrading and uninstalling.
  - [Troubleshooting](https://hive.codefrontlabs.com/docs/troubleshooting/): Fixes for common Hive problems: keys that do nothing, agents not found, protocol mismatches, odd glyphs or colours, lost sessions, and how to report a bug.
